history.period: No documented satra — Garh Ali is a historic Ahom-era road and market area of Jorhat
history.summary: UNCERTAIN IDENTITY — no web footprint found for a 'Garh Ali Satra' in any source searched. 'Garh Ali' (also Gar-ali) is the historic road built during the Ahom era (local tradition links it to defence against the Moamoria uprising; it ran from Jorhat toward the Naga Hills) and is today Jorhat's main commercial street and market (26.7568, 94.2153). A Mouthshut reviewer notes 'a beautiful temple' on Garh Ali, but no Vaishnavite satra (monastic institution) by this name is documented in Jorhat district. This row may be a CSV conflation of the Garh Ali locality with a satra institution, or may refer to a small local naamghar/satra with no online presence. NOT verified as a Hindu temple — keep-or-drop decision needed. Coordinates are those of the Garh Ali locality (approximate) and the image shows Garh Ali itself, not a satra.

town_description: Jorhat, on the south bank of the Brahmaputra in upper Assam, is the district headquarters and a historic seat of the late Ahom kingdom's capitals; it is known as the tea capital of Assam and a centre of Assamese culture and education.
